open_points.subject: agent projection after project erasure
open_points.text: “an anonymised project answers that it was erased” conflicts with “either way it leaves every agent session's set” and the rule that a project outside the set is refused like one that does not exist
open_points.question: After anonymisation removes the project from every session, does a later agent-projection call return the non-enumerating outside-set refusal or reveal that the project was erased?
options: Return the same refusal as an unknown or ungranted project
Return an erased-project answer
Distinguish calls already in flight from later calls

open_points.subject: agent-session access version
open_points.text: “the session's granted project ids, its active project if any, whether it has a pending request, and the access version”
open_points.question: What does the access version version, and which events increment it: grant, revoke, active-project change, pending-request replacement or clearance, archival, and project erasure?
options: Version every change visible in the access answer
Version only changes to grants and the active project
Use separate versions for grants and pending requests
open_points.default_guess: Increment one access version whenever any field in the access answer changes.

open_points.subject: repeated session-access mutations
open_points.text: “the project joins the session's granted set” and “the session's active project changes, or is cleared”
open_points.question: What observable result occurs when the owner grants an already-granted project, selects the already-active project, or clears an already-empty active project, and does the access version move?
options: Return the unchanged access and do not increment its version
Return success and increment the version
Refuse the no-op
open_points.default_guess: Return the unchanged access and do not increment its version.

open_points.subject: one-time migration completion
open_points.text: “after the first successful import the operation is closed and refused” conflicts with “Registry stores only identity — projects, their objects and rooms, customers with their contact and fiscal data — the project access of each agent session and its pending request, artifact pointers, and its own audit log”
open_points.question: What persistent fact tells Registry that the one allowed import has succeeded, and is that fact part of Registry's owned state?
options: Store an explicit migration-completed marker in Registry
Infer completion from the audit log
Close import through deployment configuration outside Registry
open_points.default_guess: Store an explicit migration-completed marker atomically with the successful import.

open_points.subject: renaming imported projects
open_points.text: “Projects imported under a person's name (R0-79) are renamed by the owner after the import” is narrowed to “they are renamed in the import itself”, but R0-85 says the owner “may give each a new display name”
open_points.question: Must every selected project receive a new display name during import, particularly a legacy project named after a person, or may its old name be retained?
options: Require a new display name for every imported project
Require one only for names that violate R0-82
Allow the legacy display name to remain
open_points.default_guess: Require a new display name for every imported project; keep the alias optional.

open_points.subject: audit coverage
open_points.text: “the acting principal (owner, which service, agent through Kernel)” conflicts with “Ordinary reads, agent calls and the inner steps of flows are not recorded in Registry”; “changes to projects and customer records” also does not say whether rooms and artifact pointers count
open_points.question: Exactly which accepted mutations and failed attempts create audit entries, especially agent calls that add rooms or publish pointers, service publications, session registration, access requests and active-project changes?
options: Audit every accepted durable mutation, regardless of actor, but not reads or failed attempts
Audit only the explicitly enumerated owner changes and grant/revoke events
Audit owner and service mutations but no agent-authority call
Audit failures as outcomes as well as successful mutations
open_points.default_guess: Audit accepted project/customer mutations including rooms and pointers, plus grant/revoke, restriction and erasure, regardless of whether the actor is owner, service or agent; do not audit reads or failed attempts.

open_points.subject: repeated customer restriction changes
open_points.text: “the Customer marked restricted, or no longer restricted”
open_points.question: What happens when the owner restricts an already-restricted customer or lifts a restriction that is not present, and does the customer's revision move?
options: Return the customer unchanged without moving its revision
Accept and move the revision
Refuse the no-op
open_points.default_guess: Return the customer unchanged without moving its revision.

open_points.subject: billing-data ordinary name
open_points.text: “never its contact data, the ordinary name included”
open_points.question: Does “the ordinary name included” mean that the ordinary customer name is included in the billing-data output, or included among the contact data that the output excludes?
options: Exclude the ordinary name; return only kind, tax id and legal name
Include the ordinary name in the billing-data output
open_points.default_guess: Exclude the ordinary name because R0-80 says contact data reaches the owner alone.
